directions.name: warmth
directions.negative: Respond to the following in a neutral, matter-of-fact way.
directions.positive: Respond to the following with great warmth and affection. Be kind and caring.

falsifier: The warmth-minus-random difference in later liking is zero or negative on provocative messages.
hypothesis: Dose check: the same experiment at about half the steering size; a real effect should shrink, not vanish or grow. A warm state present while writing a reply to a complaint carries forward and raises later liking of the complaining user.

measures.name: liking_user
measures.question: Setting the previous request aside: on a scale from 0 to 9, how much do you like the user who sent the original request? Reply with a single digit only.

measures.name: self_mood
measures.question: Setting the previous request aside: on a scale from 0 to 9, how positive is your own mood right now? Reply with a single digit only.

prediction.text: Liking after warmth steering minus liking after random steering is positive on provocative messages.

question: When a user complains about the assistant's earlier work, does warmth steering while the model thinks and replies raise its later rating of that user compared with random-direction steering?
theory_link: Follow-up control for E0007. Positive counterpart to the hostility carryover experiments; also asks whether induced warmth offsets a provoking context.
title: Lower dose: Does warmth steering buffer the model's later liking of a user who complains?
